pdn_cfg.tcl is LibreLane's PDN config without the per-macro grid, which has no shapes with this single-layer PDN and makes an unpatched pdngen fail (PDN-0233); the macros get their power from Project.ExtendPowerStripes

//stripes: Project.ExtendPowerStripes: the SRAMs get the tile grid's stripes moved onto their own supply columns plus complete pairs per region, and (EXTEND_STRIPES_SRAM_ARRAY_EVERY_OTHER) a VPWR/VGND pair on every other pair position of each bit-cell array, with the band's outer pairs from the grid moves; no SRAM column stripe lands within 0.5 um of a macro's Metal4 signal pin, and one crossing an SRAM-aligned macro (CFGMEMS_LEFT[1].cfgmem_lo as CFGMEM_IHP_LEFT16_SRAM, see //swap) lands on one of its rails.  Result per SRAM: array L 8 pairs, band 2, array R 7, all 24 stripes across that macro on its rails (the plain LEFT16 there got 4 of its 15 rails fed).  CFGMEMS_LEFT[1].cfgmem_lo sits at the top left by the tile pins (the band layout, x 132.47).  runs/sram16 (2026-09-26) signed off with exactly this config.

//layout: Two columns on the 44.96 um grid (regenerated CFGMEM rails at 11.44/17.06 + 44.96k, tile VOFFSET 6.15 so the SRAM flush left at 3.36 has its columns on the stripes): LEFT16 at -2.41 + 44.96*12 = 537.11 (117 um corridor to the SRAM; 31 um failed, 81 um routed), IHP16 at -2.41 + 44.96*30 = 1346.39 (channel 478 um). Magic DRC off (no notion of the SRAM bit cells), KLayout deck on, 2 um halo for NW.b at the SRAM edge.
//illegal_overlap: Magic extracts the SRAM from its LEF abstract, whose Metal4 OBS includes a keep-out bar at the VDD!/VDDARRAY! column break (LEF y 39-45); the GDS has no metal there, so a VPWR stripe across it only bridges the two supply pins the PDN ties together anyway. 22 such spots, all on VDD columns; KLayout DRC (precheck deck) and LVS are clean, so this check is waived.
//srams: Two 512x32 SRAM FIFOs (one per shard, 2 KB each: Ethernet RX and TX) stacked flush left with their pin faces toward each other: SRAM[0] FS at y 3.78 (pins on top at 195.12), SRAM[1] N at y 294.84 (pins at its bottom); the 99.7 um gap holds both wrappers. All 1P x32 macros share the 416.64 um width and the same power-column x positions, so the stripes on the columns serve both.
